_meta.recallFanoutRemoved: **Corrected 2026-10-05.** `recall.fanout` was removed from this file, from `C1` and `C2`, and from the policy itself (`packages/core/src/types.ts`, `AssemblyPolicy.recall`; `packages/core/src/config.ts`, `LEGACY_POLICY_KEYS`). It was `k`, the per-node expansion fanout of the recall walk - each BFS node expanded at most its k heaviest neighbours - and the line this file carried read `"fanout": 8`. It is gone because it was **never in the originating brief** (the prompt mentions it zero times; the brief bounds recall with `recall.depth` and `recall.threshold` only, plus `recall.window`, which it says exists only to save System-1 calls and must not affect recall), **in no record** (the tape's `kind:"wiring"` record carries `recall: {d, r, w, wait, tier1}` and no k, and this round's `manifest.json` does not name it), and **in no panel** (the plugin's `Tuning` fields are depth, relevanceThreshold, window, anchorWaitMs and tracePlacement) - so a parameter that decided behaviour lived only here, in the file whose own `provider` note says the wiring record is the authority rather than the preset. **What the round it was measured in recorded: no number of that round changes with the removal.** In `round-20261004-1239` the walk returned `candidates = 0` from invocation 9 onward, because the System-1 lane was 4.6x too slow to score the pairs and the tail therefore had no edges, so `fanout` had no effect on anything that round wrote. The rounds that did record a non-empty walk (`20261004-0233`, `20261004-1211`) stay readable and unedited: the field is gone from the policy, and a preset or profile that still writes it is read and reported rather than dropped in silence. **What replaced it:** `recall.threshold`, the brief's own knob and the one that is in the settings panel. The trade is recorded in `packages/core/src/types.ts`: on the 36.8 % of anchors where the cap did bite, the uncapped walk selects more segments (median +27, worst +69), and lowering `r` is how a round asks for a smaller block.
_meta.note: TAS off, recall selection off, chronological layout, and nothing delivered: the assembled layout is recorded, not injected. **Corrected 2026-10-05, and the superseded wording is carried here because this note is a record.** It read: "`xFirst: false` and `deliver: false` come from `cellPolicy('C0')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and are not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell." `xFirst` no longer exists, and neither does the question's position it was renamed to: `questionPlacement` ('first'/'last') lived for one day and was **deleted** on 2026-10-05, because the paper fixes the question last in every condition and `'first'` produced `[T, q, x]`, which is neither of the paper's two arms. The trace's position is `tracePlacement` ('trace-as-state'/'trace-append'), code-owned and absent from this file; an old profile spelling is still read and reported (`LEGACY_LAYOUT_KEYS`, packages/core/src/config.ts) - the question-last spellings (`xFirst: false`, `questionPlacement: 'last'`) are warned about as retired and harmless, and the question-first ones (`xFirst: true`, `questionPlacement: 'first'`) are refused with the sentence that retired them, because nothing here lays out that order. Trace placement is not an arm of this cell: **why the rename** - the paper places the question last in every condition (arXiv:2609.02702 section 4.1) and its two arms are `[T, x, q]` and `[x, T, q]` with order the only difference, while `xFirst` moved the question, the one element the paper fixes, and its name presented that as the paper's variable. `cellPolicy('C0')` leaves the question last, which is the paper's fixed point, and with TAS off there is no trace to place, so this cell records the paper's baseline `M([x, q])`, exactly as it did before the rename. **Evidence:** round `20261004-0233` recorded its order as `pinned, recalled, tail, anchor`, against the two TAS cells' `pinned, stateProxy, anchor, recalled, tail` (the question second - a layout neither paper arm has, and one no setting produces now). `deliver: false` comes from `cellPolicy('C0')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and is not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell. **Corrected 2026-10-05 (the recalled block's position - appended, because this note is a record).** The recalled block now sits immediately before the anchor, behind the tail, in the order this build lays out; in this cell's TAS-off order that is a move from second of four to third of four, so the tail is in front of the block now (in the TAS arms it was third of five, with `tail` and `anchor` behind it). That is a move *inside* the paper's long context `x`, not a move of the paper's variable: the variable is where `T` sits relative to `x`, and this cell has no `T` to place, so its baseline reading `M([x, q])` is unchanged. The block order is the table in `packages/core/src/assembler.ts`'s header, and `AssemblyLayout.order` (`packages/core/src/types.ts`) is the statement of record; neither is restated as a rule here. **Why it moved:** prompt caching is prefix caching, so anything placed behind a block that changes every step is invalidated with it, and the recalled block is the block a re-selection moves. Measured on round `20261004-1458` C2: the whole-prompt invalidation span per delivered pair fell from 2,539 to 2,111 tokens with this move, on top of the ordering change that had already cut it from 6,179 to 2,539. The round record quoted above (round `20261004-0233` recorded this cell's order) is that round's own data and is left as written, and no value in this file changed with any of this.
_meta.planGateRemoved: There was a `planGate` block here until 2026-10-02. It is gone from this file, from `C1` and `C2`, and from the policy, the schema, the status route and the report: the gate can only read a plan from a numbered list in an assistant message or a `todo/write` session event, and round `20261002-2037` - the round C2 was supposed to exercise it in - wrote **zero** `plan_gate` records into any of its artifacts across 277 steps. A knob that is on in the wiring and cannot fire is worse than no knob. The mechanism itself is kept and tested (`packages/core/src/plan-gate.ts`, `packages/dsh-plugin/src/plan-gate-runtime.ts`); `packages/core/src/types.ts` carries the full reasoning. A legacy config or preset that still carries the key is reported as an unknown key and otherwise ignored.
_meta.providerNone: `s1.provider: none` because this arm is the no-System-1 control: `recall.tier1: 'off'` disables recall *selection* but association-graph upkeep is not gated on it, so without this key the arm still scores pairs and reports System-1 calls - 363 of them (134 answered, 229 refused) in round 20261001-1300 - and a no-System-1 control has to have the lane absent rather than merely unscoped, reporting zero System-1 calls, tokens and time. Run recipe: a live profile must pair `s1.provider: none` with `laya.enabled: false`, because `laya.enabled: true` beside `provider: none` is a reported conflict (`singleBackendIssues`, packages/s1-client/src/resolve.ts); `laya` is a profile key and is deliberately not carried by this preset.
_meta.recallWindowInherited: `recall.window` is NOT set in this file on purpose, and it is **16** since 2026-10-05 (`defaultPolicy()`, packages/core/src/types.ts; the validator's floor moved 64 -> 4 in the same change). `cellPolicy('C0')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) starts from `defaultPolicy()` and toggles only `tas.on`, `recall.tier1` and `deliver`, so the window reaches this cell from the default with nothing here to override it - which also means a round reading this preset reads `w = 16` from the run's own `kind:"wiring"` record rather than from this file. `depth` IS carried explicitly above (16 since 2026-10-05, it read 2), because what a bounded walk reaches is `w x d` = 16 x 16 = 256 segments where the old defaults gave 1024 x 2 = 2048: the window's reduction is paid back at the depth, raising `d` costs the scoring axis nothing, and the validator's cap moved 6 -> 16 to admit the value. The cost this rests on is in `docs/FORMULAS.md` section "Recall window w": on round `20261004-1239` (228 segments, 16.1 questions/s) `w = 1024` offered all 25,878 pairs and cost 26.7 min of lane against a 6.2 min session - the window does nothing until it is below the session's segment count. Rounds recorded at `w = 1024, d = 2` (`20261004-0233`, `1211`, `1239` and earlier) stay readable and unedited: this file is a preset for the next round, and a round's own wiring record is what says what it ran.
